V Rising is a great game that's easy to get into. The plot aka storyline is simple and brief, with no convoluted plot twist etc... It goes straight into action mode in an open world environment. The fun part about this game is castle building and its many option. Keep in mind if you are playing in a public server you are at the mercy of that public server setting. Some server will not allow you to carry items via waygates, bat form, or even horseback. So look for a server that allows for features you desire. Castle building on a normal PVE Server typically run only 3 Castle level flooring, but on some server it can go up to six. The game only levels your character up by mean of gear, so craft the best gear you can make.

So far it seems like an incredible game. Very unique in concept with the Vampirism gameplay a la Diablo-light, while containing many familiar elements of a sandbox builder with the crafting menu.

Update: My review was Positive, now I think it needs to be Negative. This sh*t is getting WAY too hard for its own good and I'm now really having trouble keeping the motivation. Why some of these soldiers and bosses so overtuned? Are Vampires in this universe supposed to feel like limp-d*cks? The power fantasy is disappearing, and it's turning into a masochist's dream...which has a very VERY small audience.
V Rising reminds me of Diablo 2 and how mouch I loved to play that back in the day. This game is obiusly diffrent, you play as a vampire after all but I will definitly make a video about this game

*This game is awesome! It's a fully developed enjoyable experience and filled with great content!*
It's getting review bombed by people who are salty that the developer is working on a new game instead of feeding them free content until the end of time, but I assure you, the game is done, and very enjoyable.

Absolutely one of the best survival crafter / base builder games ever made. It includes free content updates even after its 1.0 release. Combat is excellent, bosses are very fun, base building is incredible. The entire game, thematically and in practicality, is just a joy to play and well worth the price.
Ah yes, finally a game in which I can be a vampire and do cool vampire things, such as... gathering resources... and ... processing resources.
This game just becomes unreasonable for solo players. There is no way of progressing without fighting overpowered bosses starting in ACT II.

Everything you could ever hope for them to have done for the full version, they basically did. This is what a good game looks, feels, and plays like. Another gem from a non AAA studio, these guys are doing what those greedy major league game companies could only dream of, DELIVERING the Gourmet. We let them cook and they did NOT disappoint. You're getting ALOT of bang for your buck here. 

The Castlevania DLC content is absolutely amazing as well, everything that a fan could have wanted them to add is in here. Highly recommend.

Decent game, feels very optimised for multiplayer but can be enjoyed solo. unique art style.

Didn't like how the game had mobile game mechanics (send off NPC for 16 hours to bring you back some middling resources), most other annoyances can be toggled off in settings (teleport restrictions etc)

Love the game, gladly did multiple saves! Have heard rumors of DLC and I highly look forward to it. Only 2 things I did NOT like is the world bosses permanently scale to your clan (?) size, instead of temporarily to the amount of active/logged in players. [note: have only played on private servers] Also, everything seems to be balanced to PvP instead of PvE, and the MOBA controls make it difficult to have a true spellcaster build.

The building and progression and fights are great tho, Simon Belmont *especially*, loved his fight. There are also lots of difficulty modifers to adjust the game to however you prefer to play!

Pros:
Combat is great fun.
Many bosses, which all feel unique.
The world feels alive.
A crafting system that I don't hate (that's rare) and even consider good (that's impossible!).
Art style and music.

Cons:
Castle decay can be very annoying at early stages of the game, especially if you don't rush through the early stage.

Verdict:
Play it.

The 1.0 release expanded on the game in a big one. It plays like a roguelite with solid survival progression and satisfying combat. I like that they spent less time making every weapon viable and more time making every boss counterable and interesting. I only have a couple wishes.

I wish they bosses had more voice acting lines so that they didn't repeat the same ones so often. I realize they use the voice lines as ability cues so you can take defensive measures, but some variation here would've helped keep me engaged in fight tension rather than detached from the same line repeating over longer fights.

I wish there was an mid/endgame unlock that allowed you to track the direction of the highest quality blood in your area. It's difficult to track certain blood times without farming out settlements as is, and this addition would've just given you something to track while you're doing that farm to cut down on time wasted hunting these blood types down.

ive played this game on another account and now im running my own server on a separate pc with that account, and replaying the game with friends using my other steam account! I have over 400 hours of active playtime, one of the best games ive played!

I love this game. Mostly been playing solo and with 1 friend (ie no PvP). Fun, interesting mechanics, and an engaging combat system. Building your own castle is great and the benefits of structuring it well add to the base building nicely. Highly recommend.

Vampires ruled the world, until Dracula was finally bested. With his dying breath, he cursed the world with his blood, his sickened ichor raining for days as many died to it, and many were changed by it. Now you, a nameless vampire, amass remnants of his power and blood for yourself to contest the return of Dracula, with the goal of taking his throne for yourself.

Still a better love story than Twilight.

A very fun game, with lots of bosses, crafting, and exploring. quite a fun game and worth the pick up. It will take some getting used to, however if you put some time in you should enjoy yourself. However bare in mind It can get very difficult, particularly on Brutal difficulty. So if you enjoy a challenge it's worth getting, assuming you take the time to get used to the controls.

I liked this game. It's kinda like Valheim! But then, a new version came out and they wiped all my progress. I thought, OK, that comes with the territory. Even though I was playing on a no-wipe server, I guess they can still force-wipe everything with a new update. I was building up everything and had a wonderful base, with great servants and literal cabinets full of 100% blood of various types, and ... all gone. On a no-wipe server.

So, I thought, OK! I'll bite the bullet and go back to my single-player game, even though this game is not designed for single-player. Lo and behold, they wiped that too. What is wrong with this company? I have never even heard of a company that automatically wipes your singleplayer character because a patch comes out.

I cannot recommend this to anyone, ever. Yes, it is a fun game. So are Borderlands 2 and Valheim. But the key difference is that they don't wipe your characters at random. This one does, intentionally, so play at your own risk.

It has some good qualities, but I cannot endorse a game this bad. Especially towards the end of the game, the controls are too clumsy for the fast gameplay the bosses need, game contains too much grinding for resources for my taste, and the lag for the servers can completely ruin the experience.

Just play it, it's worth it. V Rising has way more content than most games nowadays.

I was not expecting to be into this game and I could not be more pleasantly surprised. This game was an excellent all around gaming experience. Good balanced progression with interesting boss mechanics all the way through. It also wrapped up very nicely as a complete game. Fantastic multiplayer aspects with or without pvp. And it was also stunningly beautiful. Absolutely loved the castle building and decorating. The lore was interesting and it had easter eggs. The boss fights were very challenging, immersive and sometimes hilarious. It was challenging but not too punishing, but also adjustable in the settings if you wanted more difficulty. I really couldn't recommend it enough.
This game is amazing in so many ways. 10/10. I highly recommend playing on brutal mode for the extra challenge. The one and only flaw in this game is how rare scholar 100% blood is... best of luck!

Definitely the easiest game recommendation I can give. If you enjoy any of the following genres of games, ARPG, Survival, Base Builder, you will most likely love this game.

Having played through the Early Access version, the 1.0 release added way more than I could have expected. The graphics got a glow up, as did the UI. The visual and sound effects have been amp'd up and the game sounds more impactful than previously. The gameplay got some enhancements as well, mainly through the magic system which allows you to pick spells to your liking, and allows you to reset extremely easily very early into your playthrough. There has been a ton of rebalancing and moveset adjustments to existing enemies and V Blood bosses, while also introducing new enemies into existing factions that add more variety to combat encounters. And then the largest addition to the game, the Rifts of Mortium, are fun, not taking too much time to complete, while also introducing remixed bosses with new moves, and reward you fairly. The game does have a few bugs from what I've heard, and some visual glitches, but has been working for me without issues.

Has a very high chance to be a GOTY candidate despite being an EA game from a few years back, but if BG3 can do it, so can V Rising

I was extremely disappointed with this game. The movement mechanics feel poorly designed, and the inability to sprint makes basic navigation frustrating. Although the game offers a solo mode, it clearly does not feel designed with solo players in mind.

The combat is equally disappointing. It feels slow, unresponsive, and mediocre, with gameplay that resembles a low-quality mobile game rather than a polished PC title.

The camera angles and viewing perspective are particularly frustrating. It is difficult to see where you are going, which makes navigating the environment unnecessarily confusing. Overall, the gameplay feels poorly thought out, and the mechanics lack the quality and refinement I expect from a PC game.

I ultimately decided to request a refund. Unfortunately, this was one of the most disappointing gaming experiences I've had on PC, and I cannot recommend it. THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR REFUNDING IT STEAM!!! I Am thankful it is NOT In my collection!!!

Now that V Rising has left early access, it's easier than ever to recommend it wholeheartedly. This is one of the best co-op survival crafting games ever made. Intuitive base building, epic boss fights, and surprisingly rewarding combat, all wrapped up with a ton of immersion and flavor. I’m so blown away by the level of depth and polish they fit into this package. An extremely fun experience, one I eagerly await returning to again and again.

There's a lot of good ideas in this game but the basic implementation is just not there.
Everything is just too slow, and I mean that fairly literally, your character walks too slow, your ability cooldowns are 20% too long, your mining/woodcutting/fishing speed is too slow.
They've also clearly balanced a lot of the challenge around your character’s immobility, most of the bosses are a challenge because you just can't walk out of the way of their attacks fast enough and your dash is on cool down. It makes the game frustrating more than hard.
They also made some horrible design decisions like not allowing the player to fast travel if they are carrying resources. So you spend so much of your time slowly walking somewhere to get what you need then slowly walking back.
It's marked as early access and maybe they’ll tweak these things but as is i can’t recommend it. Its one of those games you want to like but don’t.
A fun game to play with friends. Didn't bother with the online PvP stuff and treated it more like a coop vampire romp. Had a great time.

I was recommended to play this game by a friend and so far its amazing! I really like the exploration, discovering new locations and discovering new items to help with base building. I enjoy the combat and unlocking new spells after every boss fight. The boss fights aren't annoying and it is also really easy get the hang of, once you learn the patterns. One thing I LOVE about this game is the daylight feature, many games teach us to sleep through the night and usually the nighttime is when the monsters would come out, but in this world you technically are the monster. As a vampire you stay hidden from the daylight. If you're someone who struggles to balance base building with exploration the game has a nice simple solution for you, build at day and explore at night.

Game is amazing in so many ways... but honestly I'm so pissed at the consistent perfomance issues I cant be bothered to go over them all. It doesn't matter how damn good the game is in every other way, that it is the best survival craft combat on the market, that it is some of the best ARPG combat on the market period, that it has a killer artstyle and lovely crafting and systems that all mesh together to become better the sum of the parts in a way that is truly inspired... if a fifth of your time playing is waiting for lag spikes to resolve because it maxes out your CPU you despite your CPU being better than whats reccommended by a good margin and EVERY setting being set to minimum with it having ZERO effect. You guys have no right to be thinking about new content when current content is this poorly optimized, let alone to be selling DLC with the game in this state. I get that it's CPU intensive and the reasons why... but no other CPU intensive game, many of which are CPU intensive for the same reasons and have EVEN MORE going on in terms of systems and shit it has to keep track of does this to my computer. Wait for them to fix this, then I'd reccomened it with all my heart, trying to get this game to run even somewhat smoothly will just be an excersise in frustration.

This game is amazing, when i first downloaded this game it looked ok but the more and more i started to play this game i realized how well this game was developed. The boss fights the mechanics everything about it was well developed. The building mechanics are some of the best i have ever played all the time i have put into this game was worth it 10/10 recommend if you are looking for a good game to paly with your friend.

I have lost how much time i spend time gathering and just standing in my castle just to wait for things to get done crafting, but it's fun with friends since you drag them into the mess that you are making. Also fun to name things to random things to make them laugh, just seeing a chest or something with the name that makes no sense or simply a bad joke, even naming your slaves and horse into who knows what just for a laugh.

Takes mechanical and thematic inspiration from many different places, culminating in a fun gothic survival sandbox where you get to roleplay as a mf-ing vampire. the little things and the combat especially stand out as top notch, taking a neat direction with the already praised battlerite combat and giving it a vampiric and magical spin. every one of the 37 bosses move you closer to domination, and each has a cool fight with neat unique mechanics backing them up. the map isnt random, but you will quickly forget this as its curated nature fits well with the ideas in the game, much like Ark and Conan's maps are. i would like to see some map generator in the future, or perhaps dlc maps like the aforementioned games do. but either way, you can't go wrong if you're ok with the phrase "third person survival sandbox vampire rpg with polish and killer combat".

Great fun, worldbosses that unlock powers and buildings element like Valheim, just a lot more. Interesting mechanics with blood types affecting you and their owners both in terms of enemies, and them to you as slaves or meals. The rest is what you'd expect from a survival game but done well and it's earlier.
Smaall thing to improve would be adding floors to buildings etc, and as a strictly PvE player, I worry there will be very little to do once you reach endgame, but until then it's been great fun thus far

tldr.text: Very Positive (90%): 50% of reviews praise the gameplay and combat, with players calling the loop fun.
The main complaint is that some find the mechanics boring, and the content and grind draw criticism.

details.text: Complaints about the co-op and servers have eased lately, with far fewer recent reviews raising them than before.
Very new players rate it 50% positive, while long-time players sit at 92%, so newcomers may find the early game harder to warm to.
